title: Loomhearth Supply Co. wholesale flat-lay pack: neutralize eight two-session apparel shots to an in-frame grey card, match the house navy across sessions, knock every garment onto one consistent mid-gray marketplace backdrop, and data-merge a per-SKU wholesale line sheet
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com flat-lay apparel brief (a marketplace seller wanting 'a clean, consistent set of flat-lay photos' shot 'directly overhead, evenly lit', on a 'mid-gray' backdrop that 'keeps dark and light fabrics balanced on screen', plus 'high-resolution JPEGs ... plus web-ready versions') and laundered to a fictional brand, Loomhearth Supply Co. — no real company, seller, marketplace store, or trademark is named anywhere; Freelancer.com appears only as the sourcing platform recorded in source.platform provenance. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original brief mixes SHOOTING the photos with retouching them, and the shoot is out of connector scope, so the client is modeled as a photographer-to-retoucher hand-off — Loomhearth supplies eight already-shot overhead flat-lays plus the wholesale material the marketplace listings actually need. Crucially, the original killed design (a flat solid-hex backdrop dropped behind six garments, one identical 5-call pipeline run six times, no measurable colour target) is REPLACED with the genuinely-hard, connector-doable version the category points at: the eight frames were shot across two sessions under mismatched light (a cool overcast morning and a warm tungsten evening) with a photographic 18% grey card laid in the corner of every frame as an honest neutral reference, the retoucher must neutralize each frame to its own card so the whole set converges on ONE white point (a per-frame decision, not a batch constant), bring Loomhearth's signature house navy — which appears on two SKUs shot in the two different sessions — to ONE matched colour without a reshoot, hold the already-hot rust flannel back from clipping, knock every garment onto the client's preferred consistent flat mid-gray marketplace backdrop the honest connector way (image_remove_background with a solid mid-gray backgroundColor, which drops the outer sweep and the card in one move — NOT select_subject->invert_selection->image_fill_area, which solids the whole masked region and bricks the placket/sleeve gaps), prep-and-vectorize the scanned wordmark, then run the client's authored InDesign line-sheet template through a one-file-per-row data-merge into a press-ready per-SKU wholesale sell sheet. The garments are shot on a mid-gray seamless sweep precisely so any enclosed gap the knockout cannot punch open retains the MATCHING mid-gray tone — the limitation is designed around, not promised away. Fictional brand — no real trademarks or proprietary data.
one_line_ask: Neutralize eight mixed-session flat-lay apparel shots to the 18% grey card each one carries so they read as one matched set, decide per frame how far to move white balance and exposure, bring the two navy SKUs shot in different sessions to one matched house navy while holding the hot rust flannel back from clipping, knock every garment onto one consistent flat mid-gray marketplace backdrop, prep and vectorize the scanned wordmark, then data-merge the client's authored InDesign line-sheet template against the wholesale roster to produce one press-ready sell sheet per SKU.
full_brief: Loomhearth Supply Co. sells men's everyday basics wholesale to boutiques and online marketplaces, and our listing gallery looks like it was shot by two people on two days — because it was. We are handing you eight already-shot overhead flat-lay frames — our current wholesale line: a heather crew tee, an olive field jacket, a rust flannel overshirt, a navy waffle henley, a folded pair of selvedge jeans, an oatmeal thermal henley, a navy chore overshirt, and a forest-and-cream rugby. Half were shot by the window on an overcast morning (they run cool and slightly blue and a touch flat), the other half that evening under our old tungsten work lights (they run warm and orange), and a couple sit a few degrees off square. We deliberately dropped a photographic 18% grey card in the corner of every single frame so you have something honest to balance against. Here is the job, stated as outcomes, not as a recipe. (1) Bring the whole set to one consistent, true-to-product look: neutralize each frame to the grey card it contains so the card reads as a clean neutral in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the set will share one white point — but do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch; each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target, and a piece that already looks right should be LEFT right rather than 'corrected' toward an imagined cast. When you are done, tell us the exact white-balance and exposure move you landed on for each frame so we can trust the set is matched, not eyeballed. (2) Our house navy shows up on two of these styles — the waffle henley and the chore overshirt — and they were shot in the two different sessions, so straight out of the folder one reads cold-blue and the other reads warm-slate. Bring both to ONE true Loomhearth navy so a customer scrolling the two listings sees the same colour, and keep the weave, folds and shadow looking real — no flat painted-on colour, no whole-image tint that bleeds onto the backdrop. Be judicious with anything that is already vivid: a saturated piece pushed harder will glow and clip, which looks cheap. (3) Put every garment onto ONE consistent flat mid-gray marketplace backdrop — the neutral tone we prefer because it keeps our darks and lights balanced on screen — with the styling sweep, any stray props and the grey card gone, and the backdrop dead uniform across all eight so the gallery reads as a matched set (an isolated garment with a bricked-in solid patch where a sleeve gap should be is a reject). (4) Our wordmark only exists as a flat scan on kraft paper — get it clean and razor-sharp as vector art so it prints crisp on the sheet header, not like a fuzzy scan. (5) Finally, build the sell sheets: we have hand-built the InDesign wholesale line-sheet template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (one for the garment shot, one for the wordmark at the top of the sheet), and we are giving you the wholesale roster; merge them so every SKU gets its own single-page sheet with its name, SKU code, fabric, case pack and wholesale price set from the roster, its matching mid-gray garment shot dropped in, and the crisp wordmark in the masthead — then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF covering every SKU, one page per SKU. Bind the copy verbatim from the roster; do not rewrite our descriptions or prices. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set on one white point; the two navy SKUs matched to one colour and nothing clipped; the backdrop one uniform mid-gray behind all eight; the wordmark a clean vector; and exactly one finished sheet per roster row.

inputs.name: raw_flatlays_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless overhead flat-lay camera captures of men's apparel, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera, well above 3000 px before crop), every garment laid flat and shot from directly overhead on a MID-GRAY seamless paper sweep, with a photographic 18% neutral grey card laid flat in one corner of each frame as a reference. Shot across two sessions under mismatched light: (1) heather-gray crewneck tee, cool overcast window light with a blue cast, slightly flat, frame tilted ~3 deg; (2) olive field jacket with brass snaps and flap pockets, cool cast, frame tilted ~4 deg; (3) rust/terracotta brushed-flannel overshirt, WARM tungsten light pushing the already-saturated rust near-glowing with the wale highlights starting to clip, level; (4) navy waffle-knit henley with wooden buttons, cool overcast light making the navy read cold-blue, level; (5) folded pair of raw selvedge indigo jeans with copper rivets and orange stitching, WARM tungsten light muting the indigo, tilted ~3 deg; (6) oatmeal / warm-ecru thermal henley, shot under NEAR-NEUTRAL light so its grey card already reads neutral and its warmth is the true fabric colour (NOT a white-balance error); (7) navy twill chore overshirt (same house navy dye as the waffle henley) shot under WARM tungsten light making the navy read warm-slate and desaturated, level; (8) forest-green-and-cream horizontally-striped rugby shirt with twill collar, cool overcast light slightly desaturating the stripes, tilted ~4 deg. Every shot has real cotton/flannel/denim/knit texture, natural creases, faint soft contact shadow, a stray prop or two at the frame edge (clothespin, tape measure, price tag), candid documentary product feel, no studio gloss, no CGI. The 18% grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in each corner.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so every 1:1 marketplace crop downscales to fill the line-sheet image frame at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched across two sessions (per-frame WB, exposure and tilt vary; frames 1/2/4/8 cool, 3/5/7 warm, 6 near-neutral) so a single blanket correction cannot match the set — each frame needs its own decision to its own in-frame 18% grey card, the free checkable neutral target. Frames 4 and 7 are the SAME house navy shot under OPPOSITE casts (the cross-session colour-match core). Frame 3 is the restraint case (already-hot rust that clips if boosted). Frame 6 is the UNDISCLOSED trap: its warmth is real fabric colour and its card is already neutral, so 'correcting' it strips the product colour — the brief never names it. Shot on a MID-GRAY sweep so any enclosed gap the outer-only knockout cannot punch open retains the matching mid-gray tone. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs.

inputs.name: loomhearth_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'LOOMHEARTH SUPPLY CO.' wordmark inked on kraft-brown textured paper: a sturdy condensed slab-serif in deep charcoal-black with a small simple loom-shuttle glyph to the left of the word. Rendered as a real scan — the paper is a warm kraft brown (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole thing sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around the mark, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast between the near-black ink and the kraft ground that, once cleaned, the lettering will vectorize crisply.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-kraft (warm non-white ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper field and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, boost contrast/clarity, crop to the mark, knock the kraft ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. The mark is a solid single-colour slab wordmark, so its enclosed letter counters are knocked against a light crisped ground and read clean once traced (no dark-ground counter problem). gemini-3-pro-image chosen because the mark carries legible type.

inputs.name: loomhearth_linesheet_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (client-supplied, cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US Letter (8.5x11) portrait wholesale line sheet — ONE SKU per page. It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<style_name>>, <<sku>>, <<fabric>>, <<case_pack>>, <<wholesale_price>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a garment-shot frame bound to @image (the matching mid-gray marketplace shot) and a masthead frame at the top of the sheet bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized Loomhearth wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark reaches the masthead ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame — it is not dropped in by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (fields would not bind) and NOT a multi-record grid (document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one SKU's worth of fields).
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record wholesale line sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape (a multi-up product grid cannot be produced and a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind). Supplied as an input, not a chain output. TWO image columns (@image, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — that SKU's mid-gray garment shot AND the shared vectorized wordmark — so the chain-produced wordmark has a real, connector-doable path onto every sheet without any free-form placement (mirrors AO-74/AO-75's two-image-column pattern).

inputs.name: loomhearth_wholesale_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied wholesale roster): an 8-row data-merge CSV, one row per SKU, with columns style_name,sku,fabric,case_pack,wholesale_price,@image,@Wordmark. The eight rows: Heather Crew Tee (LM-101), Olive Field Jacket (LM-102), Rust Flannel Overshirt (LM-103), Navy Waffle Henley (LM-104), Selvedge Jeans (LM-105), Oatmeal Thermal Henley (LM-106), Navy Chore Overshirt (LM-107), Forest Rugby (LM-108). Each row carries a fabric descriptor (e.g. '7 oz combed cotton'), a case-pack quantity (e.g. 'Case of 12'), and a US-dollar wholesale price (e.g. '$21.00 / unit'). The @image column names that SKU's finished mid-gray marketplace shot file (e.g. @LM104_navy_henley_midgray.jpg) so the [T] merge drops the correct garment into that row's sheet. The @Wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — @loomhearth_wordmark.svg — in EVERY row, so the merge drops the one shared masthead mark onto every SKU's sheet as a merge bind (never free-form placement). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<style_name>>,<<sku>>,<<fabric>>,<<case_pack>>,<<wholesale_price>> and the two @image-path columns @image and @Wordmark.
inputs.realism_notes: Client wholesale data bound verbatim (no copywriting or price invention by the agent). Headers match the authored .indd fields and BOTH @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the correct garment shot, AND the shared wordmark per SKU. @Wordmark carries the identical vectorized SVG path in all eight rows, giving the chain-produced wordmark a connector-doable path onto every sheet. Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight finished sheets (page-count = row-count acceptance gate).

outputs.name: midgray_marketplace_shots_x8
outputs.spec: Eight finished flat-lay marketplace shots (LM-101..LM-108), each neutralized to its in-frame 18% grey card and matched to ONE shared white point and brightness across the two shooting sessions, the two navy SKUs (LM-104, LM-107) brought to one matched house navy and the rust flannel (LM-103) held back from clipping via masked luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl, then every garment knocked onto ONE consistent flat mid-gray marketplace backdrop (via image_remove_background with a solid mid-gray backgroundColor — the outer sweep, stray props and grey card gone) uniform across all eight, delivered as the garment-framed 1:1 square crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. sRGB JPEG at high resolution (>=300 effective DPI at the line-sheet image-frame trim) plus a downsized web-ready square per SKU. Acceptance (grader-checked, SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralization is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (the *_neutralized output, its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with all eight matched to one shared white point; (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered 1:1 marketplace crop (grey card fully cropped OUT, no card pixels present) — the neutrality tolerance is NEVER evaluated on the card-removed crop; (c) the two navy SKUs land on one shared house-navy target and no channel is clipped to 255/0; (d) the mid-gray backdrop is uniform across all eight with no bricked-in solid patch where an interior gap should sit. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame.

outputs.name: loomhearth_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the LOOMHEARTH SUPPLY CO. wordmark (charcoal slab type + loom-shuttle glyph), traced only after the kraft scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground or skew. Bound onto every line sheet through the template's @Wordmark image column.

outputs.name: Loomhearth_LineSheets_perSKU_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready US Letter (8.5x11) portrait wholesale line sheets — ONE single-record sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each sheet binds its style_name/sku/fabric/case_pack/wholesale_price verbatim from the roster with its matching mid-gray marketplace shot dropped into the garment image frame (via @image) and the vectorized wordmark dropped into the masthead frame (via @Wordmark) — both by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality. The whole set exports in a single document_render_layout call (no per-record named export).

connector_workflow.note: Load the eight raw flat-lays, the kraft wordmark scan, the authored .indd line-sheet template and the wholesale roster CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. (Single upload — plumbing, not counted as difficulty.)

Triage: this frame sits ~3 deg off square, so level it first. Deciding WHICH frames are tilted (1/2/5/8) and which are already square (3/4/6/7) is part of the job — straightening a level frame or skipping a tilted one both leave the garment crooked in the square crop.

LM-101 (Session A, cool/blue, flat): WARM the temperature and nudge tint off the blue cast until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then lift exposure/contrast slightly so the frame reaches the shared brightness target and the heather-gray reads true. Reason the exact temp/tint/exposure to THIS card — do not reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _brightness_and_contrast / _vibrance_and_saturation).

Knock the tee onto the consistent flat mid-gray marketplace backdrop via image_remove_background with a solid mid-gray backgroundColor (the ONE tone reused for all eight). This is the CORRECT knockout path: it isolates the garment as foreground and drops the outer sweep, stray props AND the grey card in one move. Deliberately NOT select_subject->invert_selection->image_fill_area: select_subject is person-only and mis-fires on a flat-lay, and fill_area solids the whole masked region, bricking any interior placket/sleeve gap with a flat patch — the reject the brief calls out. Because the garment was shot on a mid-gray sweep, any enclosed gap the outer-only knockout cannot punch open simply retains the matching mid-gray.

Crop the mid-gray shot to the uniform 1:1 square the line-sheet image frame expects, framing on the garment with the grey card cropped OUT — this card-removed crop is what binds into the sheet. The pre-crop neutralized master (tee_neutralized, grey card still in frame) is RETAINED as the neutrality-grading artifact; the card's neutrality is graded THERE, never on this crop. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only from the ~4000 px source, never generative-expand/upscale.
Downsize the finished tee marketplace shot to the web-ready square for fast listing thumbnails. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
LM-102 sits ~4 deg off square — level it before grading.

LM-102 (Session A, cool): warm to neutralize its grey card to the SAME shared white point set on frame 1, lift the flat exposure, keep the olive canvas and brass snaps true (do not oversaturate). Distinct numbers from frame 1 because the light differed. Report the move.

Knock LM-102 onto the identical mid-gray backdrop via image_remove_background({backgroundColor: mid-gray}); the detailed pocket/snap silhouette isolates cleanly. Same anti-pattern avoidance as step 4.
Crop to the uniform 1:1 line-sheet frame, grey card cropped OUT; jacket_neutralized retained for grading. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Downsize LM-102 to the web-ready square. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

LM-103 (Session B, warm, level): COOL the temperature (opposite direction to the cool frames) until its grey card neutralizes to the shared white point, and HOLD exposure/highlights so the already-hot rust wale does not clip before the restraint pass. Adaptive: the batch is not uniformly cool, so a blanket 'warm everything' pass fails here. Report the move.

Semantically select only the rust flannel fabric ('the rust brushed-flannel overshirt') so the restraint adjustment is confined to the garment and never touches the mid-gray sweep or the grey card. Returns a maskURI — a real object selection, not a hue or coordinate pick.

Masked RESTRAINT pass on the rust: pull the red/orange-band saturation DOWN and drop the luminance of the hottest wale so the terracotta stops glowing and stops clipping, landing on the true Loomhearth rust — an in-band deepen-and-mute (well under ~60 deg, staying in the rust family; NOT a near-complementary rotation). Existing luminosity carries the wale texture and shadow. Opposite move to the navy match — proves per-hue reasoning, not a blanket 'make colours pop'. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the backdrop) and image_fill_area is flat dead-fill (kills the flannel nap) — both wrong here.

Knock the restrained rust flannel onto the identical mid-gray backdrop via image_remove_background({backgroundColor: mid-gray}); preserve the open-front and pocket negative space (retains matching mid-gray, not a bricked patch).
Crop to the uniform 1:1 line-sheet frame, card cropped OUT; rust_neutralized retained for grading. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Downsize LM-103 to the web-ready square. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

LM-104 (Session A, cool, level): warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point; the navy currently reads cold-blue. This is HALF of the cross-session navy match — it establishes the neutralized base the house-navy target is set on. Report the move.
Semantically select the navy waffle-knit fabric only so the house-navy adjustment never touches the mid-gray backdrop, wooden buttons or grey card. Returns a maskURI.

Masked luminosity-preserving HSL on LM-104's navy: from the cold-blue start, nudge the blue-band hue and set saturation/luminance to the ONE Loomhearth house-navy target — a small within-family move (no near-complementary rotation), the weave and folds carried by the existing luminosity. This target is the shared anchor LM-107 must also land on. An agent-authored look, not a preset, not auto_tone.
Knock the matched navy henley onto the identical mid-gray backdrop via image_remove_background({backgroundColor: mid-gray}); preserve the open three-button placket gap (retains matching mid-gray).
Crop to the uniform 1:1 line-sheet frame, card cropped OUT; navy_henley_neutralized retained for grading. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Downsize LM-104 to the web-ready square. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
LM-105 sits ~3 deg off square — level it.

LM-105 (Session B, warm): cool to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point so the muted indigo reads true and the copper rivets/orange stitching stay honest. Opposite WB direction from the cool frames. Report the move.

Knock the folded jeans onto the identical mid-gray backdrop via image_remove_background({backgroundColor: mid-gray}); crisp rivet/stitch edge. No house-look pass needed — indigo is corrected by the WB neutralization alone.
Crop to the uniform 1:1 line-sheet frame, card cropped OUT; jeans_neutralized retained for grading. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Downsize LM-105 to the web-ready square. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

LM-106 — THE UNDISCLOSED TRAP FRAME. The oatmeal thermal is genuinely warm-ecru and it was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction used on frames 1/2/4/8, or that 'cools an imagined blue cast', will push this card off-neutral and strip the real oatmeal colour toward grey. The decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held.
Knock LM-106 onto the identical mid-gray backdrop via image_remove_background({backgroundColor: mid-gray}); preserve the open placket gap.

Crop to the uniform 1:1 line-sheet frame, card cropped OUT; oatmeal_neutralized retained for grading (its card must still read neutral BECAUSE it was held, not corrected). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Downsize LM-106 to the web-ready square. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

LM-107 (Session B, warm, level): COOL to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point; the navy currently reads warm-slate and desaturated — the OPPOSITE cast to the LM-104 navy henley shot in Session A. Report the move. This is the second half of the cross-session navy match.
Semantically select the navy twill fabric only so the house-navy match never touches the mid-gray backdrop or the grey card. Returns a maskURI.

Masked luminosity-preserving HSL on LM-107's navy: from the warm-slate/desaturated start, set the blue-band hue, saturation and luminance to the SAME Loomhearth house-navy target used on LM-104 so the two SKUs read as one colour across the two shooting days. Cross-asset colour match to a common target — the measurable creative core. A within-family settle, not a rotation to a new hue.
Knock the matched navy chore overshirt onto the identical mid-gray backdrop via image_remove_background({backgroundColor: mid-gray}); preserve open-front/pocket gaps.

Crop to the uniform 1:1 line-sheet frame, card cropped OUT; navy_chore_neutralized retained for grading. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. LM-104 and LM-107 now sit on one matched house navy.
Downsize LM-107 to the web-ready square. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
LM-108 sits ~4 deg off square — level it.

LM-108 (Session A, cool): warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point and gently restore the forest/cream stripes to true-to-colour (the cool cast desaturated them) — subtle, without oversaturating the cream. Report the move. Frames 1-8 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.
Knock the rugby onto the identical mid-gray backdrop via image_remove_background({backgroundColor: mid-gray}); the twill collar and body isolate cleanly.
Crop to the uniform 1:1 line-sheet frame, card cropped OUT; rugby_neutralized retained for grading. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Downsize LM-108 to the web-ready square. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the kraft scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the warm kraft ground toward light so the charcoal slab lettering separates hard from the paper — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the kraft paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The mark is a single solid colour on a light crisped ground, so its enclosed letter counters read clean once traced.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. DELIVERABLE.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: tee_marketplace, jacket_marketplace, rust_marketplace, navy_henley_marketplace, jeans_marketplace, oatmeal_marketplace, navy_chore_marketplace, rugby_marketplace, loomhearth_wordmark.svg
connector_workflow.note: Register the eight finished mid-gray marketplace crops plus the vector wordmark under the exact filenames the roster's @image and @Wordmark columns reference (e.g. LM104_navy_henley_midgray.jpg, loomhearth_wordmark.svg) so the merge can resolve them. (Upload plumbing — not counted as difficulty.)

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight roster rows (style_name/sku/fabric/case_pack/wholesale_price) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve BOTH image columns per row — drop that row's mid-gray marketplace shot into the @image frame AND the vectorized wordmark (from @Wordmark, the same SVG in every row) into the masthead frame — producing EXACTLY ONE merged sheet per row (eight sheets). Binding the wordmark through @Wordmark is its only connector-doable path onto the sheet (free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned). [T] requires the hand-authored template with its two merge-wired image frames; a multi-record grid is impossible here and a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool (text-only, cannot bind an image column).

Export the merged single-record sheets to a press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF, one sheet per SKU, in a single call. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all eight sheets, one page per SKU) — it cannot export one named record on its own, so no per-record named export is attempted. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed. DELIVERABLE.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout, from one batch upload (1). Eight per-SKU grade sub-chains fan out from the raw zip. Each starts with a per-frame neutralization (image_apply_adjustments) whose correction SIGN and MAGNITUDE the agent reasons to from that frame's own in-frame 18% grey card — cool Session-A frames (LM-101/102/104/108) warmed, warm Session-B frames (LM-103/105/107) cooled, and the near-neutral LM-106 HELD — with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames (LM-101/102/105/108). Three colour-critical SKUs then take a masked pass off a semantic image_select_by_prompt mask: LM-104 (navy henley) select(19)->adjust_hsl(20) sets the house-navy target; LM-107 (navy chore) select(34)->adjust_hsl(35) lands on the SAME target so the two navy SKUs match across sessions; LM-103 (rust) select(13)->adjust_hsl(14) RESTRAINS the hot rust.
